units.title: Visual Language – Advanced
units.essentialQuestion: How does intentional use of shots, angles, and movement reveal a director's unique vision?
units.description: Action Crew (returning Year B students) step immediately into production leadership roles while studying advanced cinematography. Year B differentiation: Expanded Shot/Angle/Movement Scene with director's statement.

lessons.title: Action Crew Orientation & Leadership Roles
lessons.objective: Understand Action Crew leadership roles (Director, Producer, Editor, Production Engineer) and responsibilities.
lessons.notes: Action Crew students step into production leadership immediately. Groups formed with at least one Action Crew member.

lessons.title: Shot Types Review & Advanced Application
lessons.objective: Apply shot type knowledge to analyze professional films and justify cinematic choices.

lessons.title: Camera Angles – Advanced Analysis
lessons.objective: Analyze how directors use camera angles to convey directorial intent and subtext.

lessons.title: Camera Movement – Directorial Intent
lessons.objective: Analyze how specific camera movements communicate meaning and justify movement choices in planning.

lessons.title: Expanded Shot/Angle/Movement Scene (Year B Group Project)
lessons.objective: Create a scene using all three techniques with intentional directorial choices, supported by a written director's statement.
lessons.notes: Director's statement required explaining every choice. Deeper analysis than Year A project.

units.title: Production Fundamentals – Advanced
units.essentialQuestion: When you can see every technique clearly, how do you choose which one serves the story best?
units.description: Year B students deepen production skills, focusing on intentional application of all techniques learned in Year A. Action Crew duties run continuously.

lessons.title: Advanced Editing – Rhythm, Continuity & Match Cuts
lessons.objective: Apply advanced editing principles including rhythmic editing, continuity cutting, and match cuts.

lessons.title: B-Roll Competition (Advanced)
lessons.objective: Capture 10+ B-roll shots demonstrating advanced compositional choices, then edit into a 1-minute video.
lessons.notes: No faces rule. More advanced compositional choices expected from Year B students.

lessons.title: Advanced Audio – Layering & Sound Design
lessons.objective: Layer multiple audio tracks, design sound effects, and create professional audio mixes.

lessons.title: Advanced Interviewing & Documentary Technique
lessons.objective: Apply professional documentary interviewing techniques including response framing and emotional storytelling.

lessons.title: Peer & Teacher Interview Projects
lessons.objective: Produce professional interviews at an advanced level with sophisticated B-roll coverage and audio mixing.
lessons.notes: Higher expectations for shot variety and audio quality than Year A.

units.title: Music, Narrative & Story – Year B
units.essentialQuestion: What makes a film score feel inevitable — like it could only ever fit that exact moment?
units.description: Year B students study music and narrative at a deeper analytical level, with Year B-specific films and projects.

lessons.title: Music in Film – Advanced Analysis (Bruno Coulais & Coraline)
lessons.objective: Analyze how Bruno Coulais' score in Coraline shifts between the real world and Other World, distinguishing sound design from score.
lessons.notes: Year B uses Coraline instead of Nightmare Before Christmas.

lessons.title: Hero's Journey – Comparative Analysis
lessons.objective: Compare Hero's Journey structures across multiple films and episodes, identifying structural variations.
lessons.notes: Year B uses The Iron Giant + Bluey different episodes + Pixar Shorts.

lessons.title: Music Driven Story Project
lessons.objective: Create a silent short film driven entirely by music and visuals, with deliberate musical selection and justification.
lessons.notes: No dialogue. More sophisticated musical choices expected from Year B.

lessons.title: Hero's Journey Group Project
lessons.objective: Produce a group film OR comparative slide analysis across multiple films demonstrating advanced Hero's Journey understanding.
lessons.notes: Year B can choose to compare arc structure across two short examples.

lessons.title: Holiday Video Project
lessons.objective: Create a holiday-themed video demonstrating mastery of all production techniques at Year B level.
lessons.notes: Green screen required. All techniques expected at a higher level of intentionality.

units.title: Cultural Awareness & Personal Documentary
units.essentialQuestion: What does it mean to make something that only you could make?
units.description: Year B students undertake personal narrative filmmaking in their documentary slot. The Moment That Matters project is an individual silent short film unique to Year B.

lessons.title: Personal Narrative Filmmaking
lessons.objective: Analyze what makes a personal moment cinematically significant and plan a personal narrative film.
lessons.notes: Year B lesson: What makes a moment matter?

lessons.title: Storyboard Development & Peer Review
lessons.objective: Develop a detailed storyboard for a personal narrative film and give/receive structured peer feedback.
lessons.notes: Storyboard peer review required. Teacher approval required before filming.

lessons.title: Black History Month Tribute Video
lessons.objective: Create a video tribute at an advanced production level. Top videos air on the Roaring Report.

lessons.title: Women's History Month Video
lessons.objective: Produce a structured documentary about an influential woman at an advanced production level.

lessons.title: Moment That Matters – Personal Short Film (Year B)
lessons.objective: Create a 5–6 min silent short film capturing a character's significant moment. No dialogue. Storyboard peer review required.
lessons.notes: Year B exclusive project. No dialogue. 5–6 weeks. Storyboard peer review required before filming.

lessons.title: Epic Movie Trailer (Group Project)
lessons.objective: Create a shot-for-shot recreation of a movie trailer using all original footage and green screen at Year B level.

units.title: Genre, Creative Voice & Capstone – Year B
units.essentialQuestion: Looking back on two years of filmmaking — what have you learned to see?
units.description: Year B students complete their most ambitious and autonomous work, culminating in the Film Festival and End-of-Year Reflection Podcast.

lessons.title: Genre Subversion & Creative Voice
lessons.objective: Analyze how The Princess Bride subverts genre conventions and apply genre subversion to original work.
lessons.notes: Year B uses The Princess Bride as primary text.

lessons.title: Found Footage & Personal Visual Storytelling
lessons.objective: Analyze how Earth to Echo uses found footage style and discuss when breaking camera rules becomes intentional.
lessons.notes: Year B uses Earth to Echo instead of E.T.

lessons.title: How-To Video Project
lessons.objective: Create a 1–3 minute tutorial video at Year B production quality standards.
lessons.notes: Voice-over narration required. Time-lapse required. Higher production quality expected.

lessons.title: The Homage – Scene Recreation (Year B Group Project)
lessons.objective: Recreate a scene from a course film matching shots, angles, and movement with a required director's statement.
lessons.notes: Must choose from course films studied. Director's statement required. Year B exclusive project.

lessons.title: Film Festival Short Film (Group Project)
lessons.objective: Produce a 5–6 minute original short film with authentic creative vision for whole-school screening and vote.
lessons.notes: No instructions — authentic creative vision. Whole school screening. Student vote.

lessons.title: End-of-Year Reflection Podcast
lessons.objective: Create a 7–10 minute edited podcast video reflecting on two full years of production and growth.
lessons.notes: Raw recording, no advance questions. B-roll from two years of projects.

lessons.title: Film Festival Week – Whole School Screening
lessons.objective: Screen the Film Festival short films for the whole school, conduct student vote, and celebrate two years of filmmaking.
